features.name: predicted_hfr
features.note: Written by autofocus_quality_json since the write path was widened; SharedObservation carried it all along and persist_observed_frame used to drop it, so every frame captured before that fix has a null here. Null also when no FQE model is loaded — mask on it, do not impute.

features.name: sharpness_score
features.note: vision/shared_observation.rs removed focus_quality / sharpness_score / frame_quality_score on the grounds that they were 'three views of one HFR value with no calibrated meaning'. That reasoning is right and the spec's slot is redundant with predicted_hfr. The slot is held at a constant to preserve indices 2..37 rather than renumbering a published contract.

features.name: quality_uncertainty
features.note: Persisted alongside predicted_hfr. The classical path's own quality_uncertainty is documented as always None, so fqe_sigma_log_hfr is the real source and it exists only while FQE runs in shadow. fqe_calibrated says whether the sigma is a fitted predictive interval or raw between-star scatter; the two are not interchangeable.

features.name: classical_fwhm
features.note: The column exists and is always NULL: focus_agent.rs states fwhm stays None 'unless a Gaussian/Moffat fit was actually performed', and none is. focus_samples.hfd is populated but is 2*HFR, deliberately named so it is never mistaken for a fitted FWHM — substituting it would feed the model classical_hfr twice under two names.

features.name: fit_quality
features.meaning: r^2 of the focus curve fit over the samples so far
features.source: derived: ClassicalFocusSolver over samples with captured_at <= this row
features.note: PARITY HAZARD. The daemon fits the curve once, at the end of the run, and does not persist r^2. Training must therefore recompute it as a *partial* fit over only the samples preceding each row — using the whole-run fit would leak the answer, since the fit optimum is the label. Whatever partial-fit rule training adopts, focus_inference must use the identical one online.

features.name: pos_norm
features.meaning: absolute focuser position, normalized to travel

features.name: dist_from_start_norm
features.meaning: signed steps from where the run began

features.name: sample_idx_norm
features.meaning: ordinal of this sample within the run, normalized

features.name: dir_encoded
features.note: Varies only across runs that actually reverse. The agent grew a SweepPattern::Reversal ordering, so the capability exists; whether the column varies is now a collection-practice question. The plan calls for roughly one run in three — check the mix before training rather than assuming it.

features.name: run_initial_hfr
features.meaning: HFR of the run's first sample (px)
features.source: first focus_samples.hfr by captured_at within run_id

features.name: ambient_temp_norm
features.source: environment_log.ambient_temp_c, nearest observed_at within the night; join focus_runs.night_id = environment_log.night_id
features.note: Joinable since migration 007 put night_id on focus_runs — before that the observer's readings went into a table nothing could reach from a run. Present only for nights the observer actually logged, which no code can guarantee. Ambient is not substitutable by sensor temperature: a DSLR die self-heats through a session, so the two diverge in exactly the direction that matters most.

features.name: sensor_temp_norm
features.note: Populated with an explicit temperature_state of measured/estimated/missing beside it. Rows whose state is not 'measured' should be masked, not imputed.

features.name: temp_delta_from_run_start
features.meaning: degC change since the run's first sample

features.name: temp_coeff_norm
features.note: NULL until the FDF fits it, which needs a thermal night, which needs the focuser. Expected to fill in naturally; not a code defect.

features.name: filter_l
features.note: D4: no filter wheel exists and hardware/filter_wheel.rs is two todo!() calls, so the whole block is constant. The data-collection document is explicit that this block must be dropped before training and the drop recorded in norm_params.json — otherwise seven dead inputs enter the ONNX graph and the first rig with a wheel silently misuses them.

features.name: prev_delta_1
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.position within run_id
features.note: A monotone sweep makes all three equal to the constant step size; a reversal run varies their sign. Available since the agent gained SweepPattern::Reversal, subject to the same collection-mix caveat as dir_encoded.

features.name: prev_delta_2
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.position within run_id
features.note: A monotone sweep makes all three equal to the constant step size; a reversal run varies their sign. Available since the agent gained SweepPattern::Reversal, subject to the same collection-mix caveat as dir_encoded.

features.name: prev_delta_3
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.position within run_id
features.note: A monotone sweep makes all three equal to the constant step size; a reversal run varies their sign. Available since the agent gained SweepPattern::Reversal, subject to the same collection-mix caveat as dir_encoded.

features.name: prev_hfr_delta_1
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.hfr within run_id

features.name: prev_hfr_delta_2
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.hfr within run_id

features.name: prev_hfr_delta_3
features.source: difference of consecutive focus_samples.hfr within run_id

features.name: dir_changed_recently
features.meaning: 1.0 if the focuser reversed within the last 3 samples
features.source: derived from the sign sequence of position differences
features.note: This is the feature the direction head learns from, so a dataset with no reversals cannot train the head at all — not merely train it poorly. SweepPattern::Reversal produces exactly one flip per run, asserted by reversal_sweep_changes_direction_exactly_once. Verify the collected mix before training: the capability existing is not the same as the nights having used it.

features.name: steps_since_flip_norm
features.meaning: steps travelled since the last direction change
features.source: derived from the sign sequence of position differences
features.note: Same source as dir_changed_recently; with no flip in a run it counts the whole run every time.

features.name: consec_improvements_norm
features.meaning: consecutive samples whose HFR improved, normalized
features.source: derived from the sign sequence of focus_samples.hfr differences

features.name: backlash_norm
features.note: Defaults to 0 until BP-5 measures it; 0 is a truthful default here because an unmeasured focuser is compensated as if it had none.

features.name: cfz_norm
features.note: steps_per_micron landed in migration 005 and is measurable from a V-curve wing (focus_drift::steps_per_micron_from_vcurve), so this is derivable without new plumbing once a rig row exists.

features.name: filter_offset_norm
features.note: D4 again: no wheel, so no offsets, so constant 0.

features.name: background_norm
features.note: Already written per autofocus frame and joinable through focus_samples.frame_id.

features.name: saturation_frac
features.meaning: fraction of detected stars that clipped
features.note: Only meaningful when quality_json.saturation_gate_applied is true. On a body with no declared saturation_adu this reads 0.0 and means 'never tested', not 'clean' — the same D1 trap the FQE dataset builder now refuses. Mask on the gate flag, do not read the value alone.

features.name: humidity_norm
features.source: environment_log.humidity_pct, nearest observed_at within the night; join focus_runs.night_id = environment_log.night_id
features.note: Same join as ambient_temp_norm, opened by migration 007, and the same caveat: recorded only when the observer wrote it on the card.

label.name: delta_steps
label.units: focuser steps, signed (positive = move outward to reach focus)
label.note: best_position exists only once the run converges, so a run that failed or was aborted produces zero labelled rows no matter how many samples it captured. It is still worth persisting those samples — they carry valid FQE crops — but the FOP builder must exclude runs whose state is not Converged, and must never fall back to argmin(hfr) as a stand-in: the fitted optimum is interior to the sample grid and the argmin is not.
